mechanism: Ibuprofen may reduce the antiparkinsonian efficacy of levodopa by inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis and potentially competing for renal tubular secretion, while NSAIDs increase risk of GI bleeding and renal impairment in patients on chronic levodopa therapy.
action: Monitor for reduced antiparkinsonian effect and consider alternative analgesics (acetaminophen); use lowest effective NSAID dose for shortest duration and assess renal function periodically.
